sector_selloff.description: Three chip names fall together -- one story, not three.
sector_selloff.first_output:
The semiconductor names you're tracking are getting hit together -- NVDA down 6.1%, AMD down 5.4%, and MU down 7.2% -- which may be related to reports of widening chip export rules. MU is taking the worst of it, alongside headlines specifically about tightening memory rules. The broader semiconductor index is posting its worst day since March.

The Nasdaq is down 1.2% while the S&P loses 0.4%, reflecting the concentration of today's selling in tech. KO is flat, up 0.2%.

All three chip names show earnings thirty days out, which likely puts them in early to mid-February depending on when those dates get confirmed.

theme_selloff_one_holds_up.description: A storage theme sells off together; one name holds up.
theme_selloff_one_holds_up.first_output:
The memory and storage names you're tracking are down sharply -- SNDK off 8.5%, WDC down 9.0%, STX down 8.8% -- all moving together and all well below the broader semiconductor benchmark. This coincides with reports of NAND contract prices falling for a second consecutive month. MU is holding up meaningfully better at -1.2%, sitting 7.6 points above its peers in this theme despite the pricing pressure hitting the group.

Your AI compute names are tracking the semiconductor benchmark closely, down around 1% as a group: NVDA -0.8%, AMD -1.1%, AVGO -0.6%, TSM -0.9%. That's a quiet session relative to the broader decline in memory and storage.

The divergence between these two themes is the notable pattern today -- memory and storage pricing deterioration is weighing on one segment while leaving AI-focused chips largely unaffected. All eight names on your watchlist carry earnings dates around 30 days out.
